item.title: Iran accused of carrying out drone attack killing 2 Italians in Kuwait
item.description:
What to know about the Iran war today: Iran was accused Thursday of carrying out a drone attack on a Kuwaiti military facility that killed two Italian nationals. Iran denies being behind the attack.The head of the European Union's executive body responded to the deadly assault by calling for more pressure on Tehran. "Today's events are yet another reminder that security in the Gulf is a matter of security for us all," European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said.Global oil prices, which had dropped about 20% in recent weeks with the U.S.-Iran war locked in a stalemate, have risen again slightly as Tehran threatens to increase attacks on ships and fighting between its Houthi allies and Saudi Arabia escalates.
New Updates
9:28 PM
Trump says China, Russia not providing significant support to Iran
President Trump on Thursday downplayed the importance of Russia and China's intelligence sharing with Iran amid reports that Tehran's allies have helped it target U.S. military bases.
Mr. Trump, during a short press conference with reporters at his Mar-a-Lago resort in Florida, noted that the Iran conflict had been discussed during his recent trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
"My meeting with President Xi was an incredible meeting. I think that they're very little involved with Iran. They could get involved, but involvement to me would mean shooting, not giving them little information," Mr. Trump said.
He added: "We do the same thing, by the way. And you know, when they say that they may be spying on us, well, we spy on them too."

item.title: Germany arrests 2 Iraqis allegedly tied to Iran-linked terror group
item.description:
Berlin — German authorities on Thursday arrested two Iraqi men on suspicion of terrorism. The suspects are alleged to be members of an Iran-linked terrorist organization that is said to have targeted U.S., Israeli and Jewish institutions in Europe.
The men, who were arrested in Cologne and Heidelberg by the Federal Criminal Police Office, are Iraqi nationals Mostafa Al-R. and Ameer J., according to the Federal Public Prosecutor's Office.
The investigation centers on alleged links to Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya, a shadowy group that emerged to claim a series of sabotage, arson and violent attacks targeting Jewish institutions in Europe not long after the start of the U.S. war with Iran. The U.S. government has labeled HAYI a front for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and the Iran-backed militia Kataib Hezbollah in Iraq. Britain has designated HAYI as a terrorist organization.
According to investigators, Mostafa Al-R. is alleged to have maintained contact with Mohammad Al-Saadi, who is currently facing criminal charges in the United States. Al-Saadi is considered a central figure within the alleged terrorist network.
As early as late 2025, Al-Saadi, Mostafa Al-R. and other individuals allegedly founded an independent group whose goal was to carry out terrorist attacks in Germany and other European countries, according to prosecutors. Ameer J. is also a member of this group, they said.
The group planned to target synagogues in Cologne and another European city, prosecutors alleged, saying unknown perpetrators traveled to the locations in March 2026 on behalf of the organization. The plans were not implemented for unknown reasons.
HAYI is also linked to attacks on Jewish institutions in the United Kingdom, France, Belgium and the Netherlands, the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution said.
The suspects are accused of membership in a domestic terrorist organization under Section 129a of Germany's Criminal Code. ...

item.title: Could the Black Sea pull the U.S. into war in Europe?
item.description:
Constanța, Romania – Out on the Black Sea, the Romanian Navy is always on the lookout for the deadly debris of a war it isn't fighting.
It's a front of the Russia-Ukraine war that most people rarely see. It runs right up to NATO's doorstep and sometimes crosses into its waters — threatening to pull the alliance, and therefore the United States, into the war.
Incidents involving drones, mines and commercial ships are surging in the Black Sea, NATO military spokesperson Colonel Martin O'Donnell told CBS News.
"In 2025, for example, we saw fewer than 50 incidents in the Black Sea. This year alone, we're talking four to five hundred," he said.
American NATO spokesperson Martin O'Donnell told CBS News in November 2026 that the Black Sea may be "more important" than the Strait of Hormuz.
CBS News
The roughly tenfold increase threatens a major artery of global grain and fuel shipments and has made the waterway deadlier than the Strait of Hormuz, a flashpoint in the U.S.-Iran war, with both sides trying to enforce blockades on the chokepoint to exert economic pressure on the other.
Twenty-five sailors have been killed in the strait this year, according to the International Maritime Organization, while at least 40 have been killed in the Black Sea in the same period, according to the International Transport Workers' Federation.
"I would say the Black Sea is just as important, and then depending on who you talk to, some might argue could perhaps even be more important … in terms of global trade," said O'Donnell.
Any imbalance in the flow of fuel and food "can have global implications that can impact America just as much as it can any of the nations here," he said.

item.title: French actor Gérard Depardieu to stand trial on rape charge
item.description:
French actor Gérard Depardieu has been ordered to stand trial on a charge of raping an actress at his Paris home in 2018, one of his lawyers told The Associated Press on Thursday, less than two weeks after the cinema star abandoned his appeal of a sexual assault conviction in a separate case.
Defense lawyer Delphine Meillet wrote in a message to the AP that the 77-year-old actor would face trial over only one of the two alleged rapes reported by actress Charlotte Arnould.
Depardieu, who has denied the rape allegations, had challenged an investigating judge's August 2025 decision to send him to trial.
The Paris Court of Appeal upheld that decision Thursday in relation to one of the two alleged rapes.
"He disputes the decision," Meillet told AP, without specifying whether Depardieu would file a further appeal.
Arnould first lodged a complaint in 2018, when she was 22. The case has become one of the most prominent in France's reckoning with sexual violence, as the #MeToo movement has faced resistance in the country, particularly in the arts.
For half a century, Depardieu was a towering figure in French cinema.
With his hulking frame, crooked nose and commanding screen presence, he became one of the country's most recognizable cultural exports, earning an Oscar nomination for "Cyrano de Bergerac" and a Golden Globe for "Green Card."
But accusations of sexual misconduct and his subsequent conviction have increasingly overshadowed his cinematic legacy.
Earlier this month, Depardieu dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a film set in 2021, accepting an 18-month suspended prison sentence and issuing a public apology.
"I was found guilty," Depardieu said in a written statement on Nov. 16, adding that he accepted the sentence.
"I therefore offer my deep and sincere apologies to those who may have suffered," he said.

item.title: Ukraine says it downed a Russian jet-powered drone with a laser
item.description:
Ukraine has used a laser weapon to shoot down a Russian jet-powered attack drone for the first time, a senior military adviser to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Wednesday, marking a potentially significant development in the country's effort to defend cities from Russia's daily aerial attacks.
The interception was carried out using the Blysk laser air defense system, which was developed and manufactured by Ukrainian defense technology firm Carmine Sky. Technology for laser air defense systems is being developed as part of the wider Private Air Defense program, Zelenskyy's adviser Serhii "Flash" Beskrestnov said in a statement.
About 100 companies across Ukraine have joined the government-backed private air defense initiative.
Russia started deploying jet-powered drones in its attacks on Ukraine earlier this year. The weapons travel faster, making them harder to intercept than the more common propeller-driven attack drones.
In June, Ukraine was only intercepting about 57% of the jet-powered drones, reflecting a significant vulnerability as Ukrainian forces had been shooting down about 90% of the conventional Russian attack drones.
Russia has increasingly used its Geran-4 and Geran-5 jet-powered drones in its attacks on Ukraine. Come Back Alive, a Ukrainian military nonprofit group, told CBS News in September that Russia was likely to produce some 1,200 Geran-4 and 800 Geran-5 drones during that month alone, and it projected those numbers would grow each month.
A downed Russian Geran-4 turbojet-powered one-way attack drone is displayed at the National Museum of the History of Ukraine in the Second World War, in Kyiv, Ukraine, Oct. 29, 2026.

item.title: Fuel tanker explosion kills 31 on Egyptian highway
item.description:
Cairo — A massive fire on an Egyptian highway killed 31 people and injured 21 others after a car slammed into a fuel tanker truck at high speed, Egypt's Public Prosecution office said Thursday.
The driver has been arrested, according to the statement. At least 27 vehicles, including cars and motorcycles, were destroyed in the fire.
The prosecutor said the suspect admitted causing the accident while driving around 70 miles per hour on a major highway in the Al-Warraq district of Giza, which is part of the Greater Cairo area.
A fire burns at the site where a vehicle carrying petroleum products overturned and caught fire on a major ring road in Al-Warraq district of Giza, Egypt, Nov. 25, 2026, in a screengrab obtained from social media video.
Habiba Abd El Aziz/REUTERS
The driver said he was changing lanes and overtaking vehicles when the front-left side of his car struck the rear-right side of the tanker, according to the prosecutor's statement, "causing the steering wheel to slip from his hands and his car to veer off course."
When the car hit the truck, one of the truck's tires exploded, causing it to overturn and slam into a concrete barrier.
Gasoline then leaked from the tanker and caught on fire. Images of the blaze on social media showed multiple vehicles on fire as flames and smoke billowed into the night sky.
The prosecutor said the suspect was being questioned to establish the circumstances of the accident and assess any criminal responsibility.
"It was a huge fire, the cars got stuck together because of the fire," Ahmed Sameer, who was stuck in traffic behind the accident, told The Associated Press. "It was a shocking scene."
Sameer told the AP he saw at least eight bodies being removed from charred vehicles....

item.title: Andy Taylor, longtime Duran Duran guitarist, dies at 65
item.description:
Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran — whose huge pop hits included "Hungry Like the Wolf," "The Reflex" and "Rio" — and who were inextricably linked to the launch of MTV, has died. He was 65.
Taylor died following a "courageous battle with prostate cancer," his family and the band said in a joint statement posted to social media. He died Monday at his home surrounded by friends and family.
"To the world, Andy was a brilliant guitarist, but to us, he was the most wonderful husband, a loving dad and the proudest grandfather," his family said.
Andy Taylor of Duran Duran with guitars in Maison Rouge Studios in London in July 1984.
Virginia Turbett/Redferns via Getty Images
On the night he was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022, Taylor revealed that he had been battling Stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer for several years and was unable to attend.
"I would like to thank each of my brothers in this great band," he wrote at the time. "You can dream about what happened to us but to experience it, on one's own terms, as mates, was beyond incredible."
His family said Wednesday that Taylor "faced the last few years with so much courage and determination until the very end, never losing his love of life."
The two-time Grammy Award winners had nine gold records and six platinum ones, with 20 Top 20 singles in the U.K. and 18 in the U.S. They were two-time Ivor Novello Award winners and are MTV Video Visionary Award recipients.
